turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"A machine's guess. Even the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student."

I'm writing that down, Hale. So what else do you have, or is that all of it?
I don't need more proof than that.

"'I don't need more proof.' Okay."

Your own procedure, section 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish a concern. Did you speak to Owen before you entered that zero, yes or no?
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.

"Unlike some people." My child never lies. Are you calling me a liar?

I asked you a yes or no question, Hale. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?

"Zero stands." Okay. Then you'll be explaining section 4.2 to the principal, because nobody called me, and Owen found out on his phone in the middle of your class.

I'm not leaving yet. Is there a single document in front of you that isn't a percentage?
